# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-12 (Extended v103)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 3)**: (1) Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon (Friends of the A B C meeting); le Petit-Picpus convent district (Valjean, Cosette sanctuary); M. Gillenormand's residences; (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton). **Environmental conditions (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: rain threatened since morning but held off; frost silvered hedges; wind off water with salt/tar smell; roads rutted and puddled after thaw; light went early; smoke lay flat over fields; cart loaded with turnips; dog barked; chapel bell for vespers rang thinly; winter—couple fagots crackling in fireplace.

## Primary Locations (unchanged)

**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus; convent complex with garden, chapel, burial vault. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire in Marais. **CAFÉ MUSAIN**: Near Panthéon, Rue Saint-Michel; headquarters Friends of the A B C; back room with argand lamp, two windows, private stairway on Rue des Grès. **Other Paris locations**: Quai des Orfévres (engraver); Gorbeau Hovel (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Saint-Sulpice Chapel; Place Saint-Michel. **VERNON**: Colonel Pontmercy's residence; grave in Vaugirard cemetery. **ENGLISH PROVINCIAL SETTINGS**: Market towns with environmental details; river crossing at Kelmere.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette (unchanged status)

Valjean integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete—meditations on grace, humility, prayer. Cosette became convent scholar; thinks herself his daughter; adores him. Fauchelevent remains sole ally aware of full presence; grateful, talkative peasant of Picardy. Nuns do not suspect.

## Javert's Pursuit (Autumn Year 3)

Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. Investigated child abduction memory; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at door. Valjean foiled spy by silence. Old woman warned Javert lodger intended to leave; Javert waited with two men at night. Valjean escaped via cut street lantern rope (Mouffetard); Javert followed from tree to tree but did not arrest hastily. **Current status (Autumn Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades; sure convict could not be far off.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development Continues

**Identity and family**: Son of Colonel Pontmercy (Vernon residence); mother Madame Pontmercy (née Gillenormand, died 1815). Raised by grandfather M. Gillenormand (Rue Férou, then Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire).

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction: "The Emperor made me a Baron...my son shall take it and bear it." Also: "At Waterloo, sergeant Thénardier saved my life...If my son meets him, he will do all the good he can." **Lost document (critical)**: While Nicolette moved Marius's duds, medallion of black shagreen containing colonel's paper fell on attic staircase; never found. Marius convinced grandfather burned it; knew few lines by heart; paper was "his very heart."

**Intellectual transformation**: Converted from childhood royalism to passionate Bonapartism after reading bulletins/memoirs. Ordered hundred cards from Quai des Orfévres engraver bearing name: _Le Baron Marius Pontmercy_. Became thoroughgoing revolutionist, profoundly democratic and republican.

**Quest for Thénardier**: Went to Montfermeil to obey father's injunction; sought old sergeant; Thénardier's inn closed, no one knew what became of him. Away from house four days.

**Violent quarrel with grandfather (Autumn Year 3)**: Returned from Vernon third day, threw off travelling-coat and black ribbon. M. Gillenormand held one of Marius's cards. Marius declared father was humble heroic man who served Republic gloriously; died forgotten. Grandfather sprang to feet, cried all who served Bonaparte were brigands and cowards at Waterloo. Marius quivered like priest beholding sacred wafers cast to winds—impossible to insult grandfather yet equally impossible to leave father unavenged. Old man wheeled to bust of Duc de Berry on chimney, made profound bow, paced in silence. Marius went forth in indignation.

**Meeting Courfeyrac and Friends of the A B C (Autumn Year 3)**: Marius perceived in cabriolet at Place Saint-Michel by Laigle de Meaux; bag displayed name "MARIUS PONTMERCY." Became Courfeyrac's friend in few days. Youth permits prompt welding; Marius breathed freely—decidedly new thing for him. **Next day**: Courfeyrac introduced Marius to Café Musain. Whispered: "I must give you your entry to the revolution." Presented him to comrades as "A pupil."

**Intellectual distress (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Solitary by habit and taste, Marius now fluttered by covey of young men. Various initiatives solicited his attention; tumultuous movements of minds at liberty set his ideas in whirl. Heard unexpected talk of philosophy, literature, art, history, religion; glimpsed strange aspects but could not place them in proper perspective—suspected chaos. On abandoning grandfather's opinions for father's, supposed himself fixed; now suspected with uneasiness he was not. Angle at which he saw everything displaced anew. Odd internal upsetting; almost suffered from it.

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Context (Autumn Year 3)**: Revolutionary quiver vaguely current; breaths from '89 and '93 in air. Youth moulting; people undergoing transformation through movement of age. Royalists becoming liberals; liberals turning democrats. No vast organizations like German _tugendbund_ yet existed in France, but dark underminings throwing off shoots. The Cougourde outlined at Aix; at Paris existed Friends of the A B C among other affiliations.

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—the _Abaissé_,—the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Not numerous; secret society in state of embryo, almost coterie. Old map of France under Republic nailed to wall—sign sufficient to excite police suspicion.

**Meetings and atmosphere (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Convened back room Café Musain; argand lamp solemnly lighted. Nearly all present (except Enjolras and Marius, who held peace). All haranguing at hap-hazard; tossed words, caught them up in turn; chattering in all quarters. Conversations subject to peaceable tumults—game and uproar as much as conversation. Sarcasms, sallies, jests, French _entrain_ and English humor, good and bad taste and reasons—wild pyrotechnics of dialogue crossing from all points, producing merry bombardment over heads. Conversations with abrupt turns; perspective changes suddenly; chance stage-manager.

**Specific discussion (Winter Year 3)**: Bahorel and others debated bourgeoisie love of tragedy, classic versus antique tragedy, duck as parody of bird, Rue Plâtrière (now Rue Jean-Jacques Rousseau)—Jean-Jacques and Thérèse, foundlings. Courfeyrac seized unfortunate copy of Touquet Charter, brandished it, crumpled it, flung it in fireplace—paper flashed up. Combeferre watched philosophically. Courfeyrac exclaimed about number 18 as Bonaparte's fatal number—"Place Louis in front and Brumaire behind, you have whole destiny of man." Marius lowered head; cold simple word from Combeferre traversed his epic effusion like blade of steel. When Marius raised eyes, Combeferre departed; all except Enjolras followed. Enjolras left alone with Marius, gazing gravely. Marius rallied ideas, did not consider himself beaten; lingering trace of inward fermentation translating into syllogisms against Enjolras when heard someone singing on stairs. Combeferre singing as went.

**Principal members**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students, cordial with working classes.

**Joly**: "Malade imaginaire" junior; at twenty-three thought himself valetudinarian; placed bed head-south foot-north to avoid globe's electric current; felt pulse during thunderstorms. Otherwise gayest; young, maniacal, puny, merry; eccentric and agreeable. Comrades called him Jollllly.

**Lesgle (Laigle de Meaux)**: Ancestor keeper of hounds surnamed Lesgueules; king smiled at non-Bonaparte orthography, gave posting office of Meaux. Persecutions of fate rendered him inventive, full of resources. No money but found means for unbridled extravagance; once ate "hundred francs" in supper, remarked: "Pull off my boots, you five-louis jade." **Law school incident (two days before Autumn Year 3)**: Erased from roll by professor Blondeau due to misidentification as Pontmercy. Blondeau gazed with gentleness of tiger: "If you are Pontmercy, you are not Laigle." Declared himself delighted, remarked erasure saved him from lawyer profession. Made eulogium of Blondeau in death. Expressed intention to pay solemn call of thanks upon Marius Pontmercy.

**Grantaire**: Sceptic; scepticism as caries of intelligence, left him no whole idea. Lived with irony; axiom: "There is but one certainty, my full glass." Sneered at all devotion; said of crucifix: "gibbet which has been success." Rover, gambler, libertine, often drunk; hummed constantly "J'aimons les filles, et j'aimons le bon vin" (Vive Henri IV). Rights of people, man, social contract, Revolution, Republic, democracy, humanity, civilization, religion, progress signified nothing; smiled at them. **Relation to Enjolras**: Disdained as unaccepted Pylades. Harshly treated, roughly repulsed, rejected yet ever returning. Said of Enjolras: "What fine marble!"

**Courfeyrac**: Father called M. de Courfeyrac; false Restoration bourgeois belief in particle. Courfeyrac called himself plain. Wit transmitted through generations of school-attending youth. Honorable fellow; difference between him and predecessor Tholomyès very great—district attorney in Tholomyès, paladin in Courfeyrac.

## English Provincial Towns (Updated)

**Population movements and births**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead for Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton. **Rumor**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged; Ismira claimed Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (no body seen); Ismira told Luena granary fire was set on purpose. **New births (Dunstead)**: Son Ferald Stenworth and daughter Isvie Stenworth born to Luwyn Brackick. **Individuals and observations**: Harine Lindmere laughed at story nobody else found funny; "I heard river is up again," Harine remarked (Pelde said always was in spring). Rinelle fell asleep in chair before fire caught. "You look tired," Harine told Pelde Stenworth, who did not deny it. Kadrek Brackick meant to go to Ravenmere before frost but roads flooded, journey put off. Rinelle spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Kadrek Brackick complained of aching back as usual. Kassa Stenson read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Davus laughed at story nobody else found funny; asked "Will it rain?" Rinelle shrugged. **Location detail**: River crossing at Kelmere; discourse on gods, Jupiter, Cybele, Pan, Io.
